title: Prospective Identifiable Return in Associative Memory: A Completed Prospective Computational Test of Identity, Correction, Discrimination, and Reliability
lens: Prospectively frozen identity-aware evaluation of target-specific recurrent associative-memory recovery under a source-derived computational operator.
object_of_study: A fixed, source-derived recurrent associative-memory implementation exposed to fresh cue perturbations under a prospectively frozen analysis contract.
main_question: Do target identity separation and corrective recurrent dynamics jointly provide out-of-sample information about reliable target-specific associative-memory recovery beyond prespecified simpler explanations under one unchanged evaluation contract?
secondary_questions: Does ten-update recurrence recover the intended target more often than one application of the same frozen map (recurrence-specific correction)?
Does the frozen per-target reliability certificate (p_min = 0.95, one-sided exact Clopper-Pearson, Bonferroni alpha/10) hold for every one of the ten frozen targets at p = 0.05?

claim_layers.claim: External anchor: He et al. (SRC-000051, Nature Communications 17, 3096, 2026) provide the associative-memory architecture on memristor crossbars, the memristor experimental lineage, released source code and trajectory data, and the Figure-3 notebook map from which the frozen computational operator is derived (as read by the local paper). GCD terminology and the burden architecture are not attributed to He et al.

Inherited formal structure: the predecessor Paulus v1.2 (SRC-000052 / SR-OBJ-000023) supplies the distinction between identifiable target recovery and similarity or stabilization, target-specific acceptance regions and identity margins, maintenance/recovery separation, conditional recovery certificates and the 1/P cue-indistinguishability information limit, and the retrospective ten-trajectory audit in which every released cue was already nearest to its intended target. This structure is inherited, not reclassified as a new empirical result.

Prospective computational result under frozen contract PIR-COMP-2026-09-14-v1.0, run PIR-COMP-R1 (paper §14; results/RESULT_PROFILE.json): 5,711/6,000 recovery-eligible confirmation trajectories reached exact intended-target equality (95.1833%); one-step exact recovery 2,399/6,000, ten-step 5,711/6,000; recurrence-specific paired gain 0.5520, stratified bootstrap 95% interval [0.541667, 0.562504]; 3,312 trials failed after one update and succeeded after recurrence, zero showed the reverse; only two trajectories rescued an intended identity after the initial unique nearest-target classifier selected another target; frozen joint model confirmation mean log loss 0.134226 against error-only 0.175544, identity-only 0.164289, correction-only 0.160711, with all three preregistered simple-minus-joint bootstrap lower bounds positive; nine of ten targets passed the frozen per-target reliability certificate at familywise alpha 0.05; MU-01 failed with 159/200 exact recoveries (observed rate 0.7950, lower bound 0.712291); independent p = 0.50 negative control returned the intended target in 71/2,000 trials (3.55%) and the leakage audit did not trigger. Typed residuals: 76 wrong-memory captures, 201 periodic, 3 spurious stabilizations, 9 finite-horizon non-returns.

Procedural stance stated by the source: CONFORMANT for PIR-COMP-R1 — contract hashed before development, development and confirmation in disjoint randomness namespaces, primary models frozen and hashed before confirmation, zero load-bearing protocol deviations (validation/execution_receipt.json). Procedural conformance and scientific support are declared distinct by the paper (§15.1).

Identity, recurrence-specific correction, and prospective discrimination earn local computational credit within the declared object. Reliability is PARTIAL, not universal: 9/10 targets pass and MU-01 fails; the strongest all-target reliability claim is not supported. The library records this as a mixed prospective result profile, not as 'reliability proven', 'all memories reliable', 'universal return', or hardware validation.

Mechanism hypothesis (paper §16, §17.3): the combination of target identity separation and early first-step corrective dynamics is locally supported as prospectively informative for later exact recovery. Predictive support is not promoted to causal necessity, universal mechanism, or ontology.

Hardware boundary stated by the source (Publication passport; §3.3; §17.5): the study is computational; the preflight found all ten Gate-0 rows for a new hardware-prospective run NON_EVALUABLE; current public evidence does not authenticate a new physical chip/programming/calibration episode, so the completed computational run does not count as new physical memristor validation.

Canonical boundary: canonical UMCP tau_R, integrity, regime, return credit, and weld are not activated by this paper (source §2.3, §16, missingness_ledger MISS-005); the library places the object at the UMCP evaluative locus as Tier-2 diagnostic with external-ingress and domain-translation secondary roles. No GCD or Structura Reditus interpretation is attributed to He et al.

authority_boundary: This is a Tier-2 Research Library object. Library admission does not grant Tier-0 protocol authority, Tier-1 kernel authority, canon status, proof, weld, universal scientific endorsement, or physical hardware validation. The completed prospective result remains bounded to the declared computational object and contract.
scope: Prospective computational evaluation under the exact frozen source-derived operator (x_{t+1} = sign(x_t W), W = g1 - g0), ten-target registry, independent bit-flip cue family (p in {0.05, 0.10, 0.20}), ten-update horizon, target-specific exact-equality outcome rule, development/confirmation separation, predictive model freeze, per-target reliability criterion, and p = 0.50 negative-control contract used in PIR-COMP-R1.
exclusions: Does not claim universal validation of GCD.
Does not validate Structura Reditus as a whole.
Does not claim a universal associative-memory law.
Does not report a new physical memristor experiment.
Does not activate canonical tau_R, integrity, regime, return credit, or weld.
Does not claim uniform reliability across all ten targets.
Does not remove or repair MU-01 post hoc.
Does not claim causal necessity of the predictive variables.
Does not generalize automatically to arbitrary memory architectures.
Does not rewrite or supersede SR-OBJ-000023.
preserved_meaning: The distinction between exact intended-target recovery, recurrent representation correction, prospective predictive discrimination, and target-specific reliability; computational validation remains distinct from physical hardware validation.

distortion_or_substitution_risk: Primary risks are reading the prospective computational result as a new physical memristor validation; converting 9/10 target-specific reliability into an all-target certificate; promoting predictive discrimination into causal necessity or universal mechanism; treating procedural CONFORMANT status as scientific proof; activating canonical UMCP return or weld without their governing contract; or rewriting the retrospective predecessor rather than preserving the successor seam.
next_burden: Three distinct follow-on burdens remain (paper §18): (1) a separate exploratory diagnostic of MU-01's failed reliability certificate, without retroactively repairing PIR-COMP-R1; (2) a new prospective hardware-linked replication with independently frozen physical operator, chip/array/programming identity, calibration, physical-update semantics, complete trajectories, and attempt denominator; and (3) external replication of the frozen burden architecture on a second independently specified associative-memory implementation. None of these is absorbed into the present object.
repair_route: Supply the missing structure from the source work or its archive record (never from inference); if a source DOI does not resolve to the titled work, supply the DOI that does. Resubmit the same ObjectID; all seven gates are re-evaluated.
